framework.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — AI Management System
framework.description: International standard for Artificial Intelligence Management Systems (AIMS). Specifies requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an AI management system. Annex A provides 36 additional controls across 9 sections (A.2–A.10) covering the full AI system lifecycle, from policy and governance through to third-party relationships.

objects.title: Policies Relating to AI
objects.description: Annex A section covering AI policy requirements. Organisations shall establish, document, and maintain policies that address the responsible use and development of AI systems, including regulatory applicability, ethics, and governance commitments.

objects.title: Internal Organisation
objects.description: Annex A section covering organisational structures for AI. Organisations shall define roles, responsibilities, and accountabilities for AI governance including designation of an AI Owner and AI Risk function.

objects.title: Resources for AI Systems
objects.description: Annex A section covering resource requirements for AI. Organisations shall ensure adequate computational resources, tooling, and human competence to develop, operate, and maintain AI systems securely and reliably.

objects.title: AI System Impact Assessment
objects.description: Annex A section covering AI impact assessment. Organisations shall assess the potential impacts of AI systems on individuals, society, and the environment before deployment and on an ongoing basis.

objects.title: AI System Life Cycle
objects.description: Annex A section covering the AI system lifecycle. Organisations shall govern AI systems through all lifecycle phases: design, development, testing, deployment, operation, monitoring, and decommissioning.

objects.title: Data for AI Systems
objects.description: Annex A section covering data governance for AI. Organisations shall establish data governance practices covering collection, quality, provenance, bias mitigation, and handling of special categories of data used in AI systems.

objects.title: Information for Interested Parties
objects.description: Annex A section covering transparency obligations. Organisations shall provide appropriate information about AI systems to users, affected persons, and other relevant stakeholders including technical documentation and disclosure requirements.

objects.title: Use of AI Systems
objects.description: Annex A section covering responsible AI use. Organisations shall ensure AI systems are used responsibly, with appropriate human oversight, safeguards against misuse, and mechanisms for individuals to contest automated decisions.

objects.title: Third-Party and Customer Relationships
objects.description: Annex A section covering third-party AI governance. Organisations shall manage AI-related risks arising from third-party AI providers, suppliers, and customers, including contractual obligations, due diligence, and shared responsibility frameworks.

objects.title: AI Policy Framework
objects.description: Organisations shall establish, document, and maintain an AI policy framework that defines the organisation’s approach to AI governance, ethical principles, regulatory applicability (including the EU AI Act and sector-specific obligations), and management commitments. The policy shall be approved by top management and communicated to all relevant parties.

objects.title: AI Roles and Responsibilities
objects.description: Organisations shall define and assign roles and responsibilities for AI governance, including an AI Owner, AI Risk function, and accountability structures for AI system decisions. Reporting lines and escalation paths shall be documented and communicated.

objects.title: AI System Resources
objects.description: Organisations shall ensure the availability of adequate resources for AI systems, including computational infrastructure, tooling environments, personnel competence, and access to verified training datasets. Resource constraints that could affect system reliability or safety shall be identified and managed.

objects.title: AI System Impact Assessment
objects.description: Organisations shall conduct structured impact assessments for AI systems before deployment and periodically thereafter, covering risks to individuals, groups, society, and the environment. Assessments shall identify potential harms, evaluate likelihood and severity, and define mitigation measures. High-risk AI systems require formal Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIA).

objects.title: AI Development Governance
objects.description: Organisations shall establish governance controls for the development of AI systems, including design specifications, model selection criteria, testing requirements, security reviews, and approval gates before deployment. Development practices shall incorporate responsible AI principles and bias mitigation from the outset.

objects.title: AI System Lifecycle
objects.description: Organisations shall manage AI systems through their full lifecycle, including operational monitoring, performance degradation detection, incident response, change management, and planned decommissioning. Post-deployment monitoring shall include drift detection, anomaly detection, and feedback loops for continuous improvement.

objects.title: Data for AI Systems
objects.description: Organisations shall establish data governance practices for AI systems covering data collection and provenance, data quality assurance, bias detection and mitigation, handling of special categories of personal data, and data lineage documentation. Training, validation, and test datasets shall meet defined quality thresholds.

objects.title: Information for Interested Parties
objects.description: Organisations shall provide appropriate, timely, and accessible information about AI systems to all relevant interested parties, including technical documentation for regulators, plain-language disclosures for users, and notifications to affected persons. Information shall cover system purpose, capabilities, limitations, and data handling practices.

objects.title: Responsible Use of AI Systems
objects.description: Organisations shall ensure AI systems are used responsibly and in accordance with their intended purpose. Controls shall include human oversight mechanisms, override capabilities, safeguards against misuse, and rights for individuals to contest, request review of, or opt out of AI-driven decisions that significantly affect them.

objects.title: Third-Party and Customer Relationships
objects.description: Organisations shall manage AI-related risks arising from third-party AI systems, component suppliers, and AI service providers. Contractual arrangements shall address data handling, model behaviour, liability, audit rights, and ongoing monitoring. Organisations shall also define obligations when supplying AI systems to customers.
